The verb beset is followed by the preposition “with”, meaning to be troubled or plagued by something.
✔ Correct usages:



The project is beset with difficulties.


The country was beset with internal conflicts.

t: The proposal was neither practical nor financially viable, ______?
e: The Correct Ans is Option (c) - “was it”. 📌 Rule / Concept: “Neither…nor” = Negative Meaning + Auxiliary Repetition The correlative conjunction “neither…nor” makes the sentence negative in meaning. When the statement is negative → the question tag must be positive. Also, when the main clause already contains an auxiliary verb (was/were/is/has etc.), we must repeat that auxiliary in the tag. 💢 Application to the Given Question The proposal was neither practical nor financially viable “Neither…nor” → negative meaning Therefore → tag must be positive Auxiliary used = was Subject = “The proposal” → replaced by it So, the correct tag is: was it? ✅ More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅- The report was neither accurate nor complete, was it? Example 2 ✅- The policy is neither feasible nor affordable, is it? Example 3 ✅ - The solution was neither efficient nor sustainable, was it? 🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips “Neither…nor” → treat as negative statement. Negative meaning → positive tag. Repeat the same auxiliary. Do not be confused by two adjectives — focus on polarity.

t:
Select the appropriate option for the given blank-
Water _____ at 0 degrees Celsius.
e: It is a fact about water. So, the use of 'freezes' is correct as present indefinite tense. The correct sentence is- Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius. Hence, option (a) is correct.

t: The medical board’s primary requirement is that every resident doctor __________ at least twelve hours of rest between consecutive shifts to ensure patient safety and minimize clinical errors.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B). 📌 Rule / Concept: The Mandative Subjunctive (Noun Triggers) The Present Subjunctive mood is used in "that-clauses" following not only specific verbs and adjectives but also nouns that express a requirement, necessity, or demand (such as requirement, suggestion, recommendation, order, insistence). In this mood, the verb must be in its base form, regardless of the subject's person or number. 💢 Application to the Given Question - The noun requirement followed by "that" triggers the subjunctive mood. Even though the subject "every resident doctor" is singular and would typically take the indicative verb "takes," the presence of the subjunctive trigger requires the base form take. More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅ The requirement that he be present is non-negotiable. Example 2 ✅ Her suggestion that the team work on weekends was rejected. Example 3 ✅ It is a demand of the law that every driver possess a valid license.

t: Little progress has been made despite repeated assurances from the authorities, ______?
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B) - “has it”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Negative Meaning Word (“Little”) + Auxiliary Repetition The word “little” (without “a”) carries a negative meaning (almost none). When a statement is negative in meaning → the question tag must be positive. Also, when the main clause contains an auxiliary verb (has/have/is/was etc.), we must repeat that auxiliary in the tag. 💢 Application to the Given Question “Little progress” → negative meaning Therefore → tag must be positive The auxiliary used is has Subject “progress” → replaced by it So, the correct tag is: has it? ✅ More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅- Little improvement has occurred, has it? Example 2 ✅ - Little attention was paid to the issue, was it? Example 3 ✅ - Little effort has been shown so far, has it? 🧠 Things to Remember “Little” (without “a”) = negative meaning. Negative meaning → positive tag. Repeat the same auxiliary from the main clause. Do not get confused between “a little” (positive meaning) and “little” (negative meaning).

t: Had the central authority ____ immediate corrective measures during the fiscal deficit, several state-run enterprises ____ into insolvency proceedings.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B)👉 Replace the blanks with “taken / would have plunged”.📌 Rule / Concept: Inversion in Third Conditional (Without “If”)Structure: Had + subject + V3, would have + V3This is equivalent to: If the central authority had taken…✅ More ExamplesExample 1 ✅- Had the bank acted earlier, the crisis would have been avoided.Example 2 ✅- Had she informed us, we would have responded.Example 3 ✅- Had the audit been stricter, the fraud would have been detected.

t: The board of directors is unlikely to reverse its decision at this stage, ______?
e: The Correct Ans is Option (A) - “isn’t it”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Collective Noun Agreement + Auxiliary Consistency In formal competitive exam English, collective nouns such as board, committee, jury, panel are generally treated as singular unless emphasis is on individual members. The auxiliary used in the tag must: Match the tense of the main verb. Agree with the grammatical number of the subject. 💢 Application to the Given Question - The subject is “The board of directors”. The core subject is “board”, which is singular. The verb used is “is” (present tense). So the tag must be: Negative (because statement is positive) Singular Use same auxiliary “is” Hence: isn’t it? is the correct answer. ✅ More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅ - The committee is reviewing the proposal, isn’t it? Example 2 ✅ - The jury has reached its verdict, hasn’t it? Example 3 ✅ - The panel is considering the appeal, isn’t it? 🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips Identify the real subject (board, committee, panel). SSC usually treats collective nouns as singular. Match the auxiliary exactly (is → isn’t). Avoid being misled by the plural noun after “of”.

t: Each of the applicants has fulfilled the eligibility criteria, ______?
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B) - “hasn’t he”. 📌 Rule / Concept: “Each of” + Singular Agreement in Question Tags When a sentence begins with: Each of + plural noun The grammatical subject is “each”, not the plural noun. “Each” is singular, so: The verb must be singular The tag pronoun must also be singular In traditional formal competitive exams, the singular pronoun “he” is preferred in tags. 💢 Application to the Given Question Each of the applicants has fulfilled the eligibility criteria Real subject = Each (singular) Verb used = has (correct singular auxiliary) Statement is positive → tag must be negative Pronoun must agree with “each” → singular Therefore: hasn’t he? ✅ More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅- Each of the students has submitted the form, hasn’t he? Example 2 ✅- Each of the officers was present, wasn’t he? Example 3 ✅- Each of the candidates has cleared the test, hasn’t he? 🧠 Things to Remember “Each of” → subject is singular. Ignore the plural noun after “of”. Verb and tag must be singular. SSC usually prefers singular pronoun in such cases.

t: We have not yet been able to explain whether x = y. A larger sample ______ us to make more accurate predictions, and this is why we are beginning sampling again.
e:
The Correct Ans is Option (B)

👉 Replace “_____” with “would enable”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Conditional Sense with Present–Future Reference

This sentence tests conditional meaning based on time reference, not a fixed “if-clause” structure.

When a sentence discusses a current limitation and a future-oriented plan, English uses:

would + base verb to express a hypothetical or potential result that is still achievable.

Key examiner logic:

 


 would + base verb → possible, unreal but still open
 would have + past participle → past unreal, opportunity already lost


💢 Application to the Given Question

“A larger sample _____ us to make more accurate predictions, and this is why we are beginning sampling again.”

 


 “have not yet been able” → the issue is still unresolved
 “this is why we are beginning sampling again” → action is starting now / future
 Therefore, the enabling condition is not finished in the past


Using would have enabled would incorrectly suggest:


 The larger sample existed earlier
 The chance to improve predictions is already over

 This directly contradicts the reason clause.

t: There were very few objections raised during the stakeholder consultation, ______?
e: The Correct Ans is Option (B) - “were there”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Negative Meaning Words (Very Few) + There Construction This sentence follows a specific rule for negative adverbs “Very few” carries a negative meaning (almost none). When a sentence is negative in meaning, the question tag must be positive. Also, in there constructions, the tag must use “there”, not the noun. 💢 Application to the Given Question - “Very few” → negative in meaning. So the tag must be positive → were there? ✅ More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅- There are very few options left, are there? Example 2 ✅ - There was little progress, was there? Example 3 ✅ - There were hardly any complaints, were there? 🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips Very few / little → negative meaning Negative meaning → positive tag In “there” sentences → tag must use “there”

t: Let’s reassess the projected liabilities before presenting the draft budget, ______?
e: The Correct Ans is Option (C) - “shall we?”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Let’s Construction in Question Tags When a sentence begins with “Let’s” (Let us), the correct question tag is : shall we? This is a fixed grammatical structure in English. ✅ More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅- Let’s begin the meeting, shall we? Example 2 ✅ -Let’s review the policy framework again, shall we? Example 3 ✅- Let’s postpone the discussion, shall we?

t:
Select the appropriate option for the given blank.
The boy ______ the blood on his knee.
e:
The blank requires a transitive verb to be used along with object of the sentence 'the blood'. Accordingly, all the options except option (c), 'wiped' are intransitive verbs and so, they are negated.
The complete sentence is: The boy wiped the blood on his knee.
Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

t: I apprised him..........the serious food situation in the state.
e:
The verb apprise means to inform and is followed by the preposition “of.”
✔ Correct usages:



He was apprised of the facts.


She apprised the committee of the risks involved.

t: The following sentence contains blank spaces, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.The billionaire was renowned for his impeccable ___________ classical art, yet he surprisingly possessed no ___________ the ostentatious lifestyle that usually accompanies such wealth.
e: Rule / Concept: Taste in vs. Taste forIn high-level English, "Taste" takes different prepositions depending on whether you are talking about judgment and standards or a personal desire and appetite:Application to the Given Question"...renowned for his impeccable taste in classical art, yet he surprisingly possessed no taste for the ostentatious lifestyle..."In the first part, the billionaire’s ability to judge and select high-quality "classical art" refers to his aesthetic standards, requiring "in". In the second part, the "ostentatious lifestyle" refers to a desire or appetite for a certain way of living, requiring "for". The original option flipped these, creating a contextual error.Things to Remember / Exam Tips

t:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
Wolves howl to communicate ________ location to other pack members and to ______ off rivalling packs from their territory, it's also been ________ that wolves will howl to their own pack members out of affection, as opposed to anxiety, wolf packs tend to ________ large territories for themselves, especially if prey is scarce.
e:
The use of 'there' and 'our' is incorrect to talk about wolves. So, options (b) and (d) will get eliminated.
'Ward off' is the right phrasal verb which means to prevent someone or something from harming or affecting one. Therefore, it is used in the sentence to talk about the harm that rivalling packs can cause.
Hence, option (a) is correct.

t:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.
Savita was crying ______ as she felt that her world had fallen apart due to the accident.
e: Mildly - in a mild or gentle manner/ not seriously Bitterly - in a way that shows strong negative emotion such as anger or disappointment Definitely - without doubt (used for emphasis). Hardly - scarcely (used to qualify a statement by saying that it is true to an insignificant degree). The sentence implies that Savita was crying because she felt as if her world had fallen apart. If someone's world or life falls apart, something very bad and serious happens which changes their life. Among the given options, only 'bitterly' fits the blank, contextually, the best. The correct sentence is: Savita was crying bitterly as she felt that her world had fallen apart due to the accident. Hence, option (b) is the answer.

t: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. The diver watched in awe as a sleek _____ gracefully glided through the water.
e:
The given sentence describes a sleek creature gracefully gliding through the water, which fits the behaviour of a 'seal', a marine mammal. Hence, (b) is the correct answer. 
The final sentence: The diver watched in awe as a sleek seal gracefully glided through the water. 
"Cell" refers to the smallest structural and functional unit of an organism.
"Sell" means to exchange goods or services for money.
"Ceil" refers to the overhead interior surface of a room.

t: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. The strict policy does not __________ any deviation from the prescribed procedure.
e: Explanation: The correct answer is option (2). English Explanation: “Allow of” is a formal expression meaning to permit or make something possible, and it is most commonly used in negative constructions such as “does not allow of.” In the sentence, “The strict policy does not ______ any deviation,” the meaning clearly suggests that no deviation is permitted. Therefore, “does not allow of” correctly conveys that there is no scope for exceptions. “Allow for” means to take something into consideration. “Allow in” means to permit someone to enter. “Allow through” means to permit someone or something to pass. Since the context is about permitting or not permitting exceptions, “allow of” is the most appropriate fit. 1. Allow for (ध्यान में रखना / गुंजाइश रखना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी बात को ध्यान में रखना या संभावना को शामिल करना। Example: We must allow for traffic delays while planning the trip. (यात्रा की योजना बनाते समय हमें ट्रैफिक की देरी को ध्यान में रखना चाहिए।) 2. Allow of (अनुमति देना / संभव बनाना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी चीज़ की अनुमति देना, विशेषकर औपचारिक संदर्भ में। Example 1: The rules do not allow of any relaxation in the age limit for this examination. (नियम इस परीक्षा में आयु सीमा में किसी भी प्रकार की छूट की अनुमति नहीं देते।) Example 2: The situation does not allow of further discussion. (स्थिति आगे चर्चा की अनुमति नहीं देती।) 3. Allow in (अंदर आने देना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी को अंदर प्रवेश करने की अनुमति देना। Example: The guard allowed the visitors in after checking their IDs. (गार्ड ने पहचान पत्र जांचने के बाद आगंतुकों को अंदर आने दिया।) 4. Allow through (गुजरने देना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी को या किसी वस्तु को पार होने की अनुमति देना। Example: The security check allowed only authorized vehicles through. (सुरक्षा जांच ने केवल अधिकृत वाहनों को गुजरने दिया।)

t: Ethical conduct in public and private life is often tested not during moments of convenience but in situations that demand personal sacrifice. While individuals may profess strong moral beliefs, real commitment becomes evident when actions involve [--1---] consequences rather than symbolic gestures. In professional environments, ethical lapses are frequently justified as pragmatic compromises, yet such reasoning can gradually [-----2----] moral accountability. Over time, repeated rationalization of minor transgressions fosters a climate of [----3---] indifference, where wrongdoing is normalized rather than questioned. Scholars therefore argue that ethical integrity must be sustained through a [---4----] adherence to values, independent of external reward or recognition. Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [1] :
e: Inconvenient refers to actions that cause discomfort or personal cost. The passage contrasts genuine ethical commitment with easy symbolism, indicating that true morality is tested when choices are difficult and personally demanding. WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG • Incidental suggests accidental or minor consequences. • Hypothetical refers to imagined situations, not real action. • Ornamental implies decorative or showy gestures, which the sentence rejects.

t:
In the following question, the sentence is given with a blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the five and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. 
He was hoping __________ hope that the thief will bring his wallet back to him.
e: " The correct options is (3) i.e.  against Option 1 ‘for’ cannot be used because someone can’t hope for hope again. ‘In’ cannot be used in the blank since it does not fit in the context. Till cannot be used as it is used to define an ending period and the statement does not indicate any such period. ‘Towards’ meaning to aim at something, but such an aim is not present in the statement. Only, ‘against’ fits the context as it means to hope in a little way against all possibilities, and hence, it is the proper fit. Note: 'To hope against hope' is a phrase that means 'to hope for something that is almost impossible'.  "

t: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. The recent statistics clearly __________ the researcher’s hypothesis about rising inflation.
e: Explanation: The correct answer is option (3). English Explanation: “Bear out” means to confirm, support, or prove that something is true, usually with evidence or facts. In the sentence, the recent statistics are supporting or proving the researcher’s hypothesis about rising inflation. Therefore, “bear out” correctly conveys the idea of confirming a claim with evidence. “Bear up” means to remain strong during difficulty. “Bear down” means to apply pressure or concentrate intensely. “Bear with” means to be patient with someone. Since the context refers to evidence confirming a hypothesis, “bear out” is the most appropriate fit. 1. Bear up (हिम्मत बनाए रखना) Meaning in Hindi: कठिन परिस्थितियों में मजबूत बने रहना। Example: She bore up well despite the challenges. (चुनौतियों के बावजूद उसने हिम्मत बनाए रखी।) 2. Bear down (दबाव डालना / ज़ोर लगाना) Meaning in Hindi: पूरी ताकत लगाना या दबाव बनाना। Example: The lawyer bore down on the witness with tough questions. (वकील ने गवाह पर कठिन प्रश्नों के साथ दबाव डाला।) 3. Bear out (पुष्टि करना / सही साबित करना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी दावे या कथन की पुष्टि करना। Example 1: The data collected from the survey bears out the claim that unemployment has increased. (सर्वे से एकत्रित आँकड़े इस दावे की पुष्टि करते हैं कि बेरोज़गारी बढ़ी है।) Example 2: The results bore out his prediction. (परिणामों ने उसकी भविष्यवाणी को सही साबित किया।) 4. Bear with (धैर्य रखना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी के साथ धैर्य रखना या प्रतीक्षा करना। Example: Please bear with me while I fix this issue. (कृपया इस समस्या को ठीक करते समय धैर्य रखें।)

t: The following sentence contains blank spaces, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.In a desperate attempt to get the lifeguard's attention, the drowning man _________ his waterproof watch _________ the pier, hoping someone would notice it, while the rescuers _________ a lifebuoy _________ him.
e: RuleApplication to the Given Question"...drowning man [1] threw his waterproof watch AT the pier... rescuers [2] threw a lifebuoy TO him."First Blank: The man isn't "passing" the watch for the pier to catch it. He is aiming at a physical target (the pier) to create a noise or signal. This is "targeting" a spot, which requires at.Second Blank: The rescuers want the man to catch the lifebuoy so he can be saved. This is a cooperative action, requiring to.

t:
Select the most appropriate homonyms from the given alternatives to fill in the blanks. 
I didn't ______ to be ______ when I said that.
A. mean (average)
B. mean (verb)
C. mean (cruel)
e: Mean (verb) is appropriate in the first blank as it refers to the act of conveying an idea or intention: "I didn't mean to be..." Mean (cruel) fits the context when placed in second blank as it refers to being unkind: "to be mean when I said that." The words in their respective places give the meaning that the speaker didn't intend to be unkind. Mean (average) does not fit the context of the sentence, as it relates to a statistical concept. The correct sentence is: I didn't mean to be mean when I said that. Hence, option (a) is the answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate homophone of the underlined word to fill in the blank.
She had to <u>write</u> a report tomorrow. The report is about the ancient _______ of the Egyptians.
e:
The most appropriate homophone of the underlined word to fill in the blank is 'rite'. This word means a religious or other solemn ceremony or act. It is also an apt homophone of 'write', which means to mark letters, words, or symbols on a surface, typically paper, with a pen, pencil, or similar implement. 'Right' means correct or morally good/a moral or legal entitlement to have or do something, 'wright' means a maker or builder, and 'straight' means continuing in one direction without bending or curving.
'Rights' [legal, social, or ethical principles of freedom or entitlement] would have been correct in place of 'right'.
Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

t:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.
Towel off and _____ your moisturizer immediately.
e:
The blank requires a verb that denotes an action with respect to moisturizer.
Apply - to spread or rub a substance such as cream or paint on a surface.
So, only 'apply' fits in contextually and implies that the speaker asks for the moisturizer to be spread or rub.
Hence, option (d) is the answer.
The complete sentence is: Towel off and apply your moisturizer immediately.
Surrender - stop resisting to an enemy or opponent and submit to their authority.

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s).
An illness is a particular abnormal ________ that ________ affects the structure or _______ of all or part of an organism, and that is not immediately due to _____ external injury.
e:
The paragraph talks about the illness and its effects.
In the first blank, all the words can be used to talk about the abnormality, except for the one mentioned in option (b), 'abnormal prime' does not make a meaningful phrase.
In the second blank, an adverb will be used to qualify the verb 'affects', so the use of 'death' (being a noun) is incorrect. So, option (c) is eliminated.
In the third blank, a noun is required to talk about the entities that are being affected due to illness, so the use of 'edifice' is incorrect because 'edifice' means a large, impressive building, so it does not go with the given context.
In the fourth blank, the use of 'any' is accurate to talk about whatever kind of injury.
'Condition, negatively, function, any' is the right set of words for the blanks.
Hence, option (d) is correct.

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Astronomy enthusiasts and sky gazers will be able to watch six eclipses in 2020, but only three of them are expected to be ______ in India.
e:
The blank requires an adjective that indicates the presence of eclipses in India. 'Exposed' (make (something) visible by uncovering it), 'evident' (clearly seen or understood; obvious) and 'revealed' (cause or allow (something) to be seen) are contextually irrelevant options to the sentence and thus negated. 'Visible' means 'able to be seen' which denotes how the eclipses will be in India.
Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

t:
Select the correct homonym from the given options to fill in the blank.
This _____ is grown in our garden.
e:
The blank requires a noun that denotes something that is grown in a garden. Accordingly, 'gourd' (a fleshy, typically large fruit with a hard skin, some varieties of which are edible) is the most appropriate word that matches the context of the sentence and can fill the blank.
GORD- short for gastro-oesophageal reflux disease.
Guard- a person who keeps watch, especially a soldier or other person assigned to protect a person or to control access to a place.
Gaud - a showy and purely ornamental thing.
The complete sentence is: This gourd is grown in our garden.
Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s).
The marquee on ______ closed neighbourhood movie theatre reads, "See you on the other side; I like reading it every day as I pass by on ______ walk.
e: 'My' is a possessive adjective and 'mine' is a possessive pronoun. You use a possessive adjective where you already have a noun (such as neighbourhood and walk) and want to modify and indicate ownership of the noun. Like with all pronouns, you use a possessive pronoun in place of another noun when it's understood what's being discussed or what is the main noun. 'My' will be used in both the blanks as both the blanks are followed by nouns. Option A is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Accepting how wonderful you truly are and incorporating this _______ into your attitude and personality is perhaps one of the most difficult things to do in life.
e:
"Insight" means a deep understanding of something, fitting the context of recognizing and incorporating one's true worth into one's attitude. So, it can fill in the given blank in the sentence.
Craziness: Incorrect, as it implies irrationality, not self-awareness.
Folly: Incorrect, as it means foolishness, not a positive realization.
Glitch: Incorrect, as it refers to a technical error, not personal understanding.
The complete sentence: Accepting how wonderful you truly are and incorporating this insight into your attitude and personality is perhaps one of the most difficult things to do in life.
Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

t:
Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. 
The farmer harvested a bountiful crop of ____ from his field.
e: "Maize" is the correct homonym for this sentence. Maize is a type of cereal grain, also known as corn in some regions. It is a common crop harvested by farmers. So, the correct answer is (b) 'Maize', as it is the word that fits the context of harvesting a crop in a field. The complete sentence is: The farmer harvested a bountiful crop of maize from his field. The rest of the words don't fit in contextually. Mace - a spice made from the dried shell of nutmeg/ a decorated rod that is carried by or put in front of particular public officials as a symbol of their authority. Maze - a network of paths and hedges designed as a puzzle through which one has to find a way. Mase - something that causes bewilderment or mystery.

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
As I review the events of my past life, I realise how________ are the influences that shape our destinies.
e:
Let's look at the meanings of the given words.
Subtle: (especially of a change or distinction) so delicate or precise as to be difficult to analyse or describe.
Crude: constructed in a rudimentary or makeshift way.
Plain: not decorated or elaborate; simple or basic in character.
Artless: without guile or deception.
The given sentence talks about the influences that shape our destiny. The blank should be replaced with an adjective that can qualify the noun 'influences'. Among the given options, only 'subtle' can replace the blank as its use conveys that even the smallest influence can shape our destiny.
Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. 
The homophone for the word "scene" is _______.
e: A homophone is a word that sounds the same as another word but has a different meaning and often a different spelling. Scene (a setting or part of a play or event) and seen (the past participle of "see") are pronounced the same way but have different meanings, making them homophones. Hence, option (d) is the answer. Sane - mentally stable. Seem - to appear to be. Send - to dispatch something.

t:
Select the most appropriate homophones to fill in the blanks.
He had ___________ his ___________ in the pond and watched the ripples.
e: Option (b) is the correct choice. Thrown is a verb which means to propel something with force through the air by a movement of the arm and hand. A throne is a ceremonial chair for a sovereign, bishop, or similar figure. The sentence is about a person who propelled his ceremonial chair in the pond and watched the ripples.

t:
Select the most appropriate article(s) to fill in the blanks. 
Every ____ year, many people all over ____ world need new organs to continue enjoying their lives.
e: The phrase "every year" does not require an article in between because "every" itself conveys a sense of regularity and encompasses all years in a recurring manner. Adding "a" or "an" would be incorrect, as "every" already provides the necessary grammatical structure. So, no article is required in the first blank. The definite article "the" should be used in the second blank because "world" is unique and universally understood as a specific entity. There is only one world being referred to here, so "the" is appropriate. The complete sentence is: Every year, many people all over the world need new organs to continue enjoying their lives. Hence, option (a) is the answer. Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun or plural noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun or singular noun.

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Timers at traffic signals, that help motorists save fuel by switching off their engines while waiting, will soon be phased out due to technical ______.
e:
Let's look at the meanings of the given words.
Symbols: a sign, shape, or object that is used to represent something else.
Glitches: a small problem or fault that prevents something from being successful or working as well as it should.
Illuminations: coloured decorative lights outside that make a town look bright and exciting at night.
Streamers: a long, narrow strip of brightly coloured paper that is used as a decoration for special occasions such as parties.
The verb 'phased out' means 'to discontinue the practice, production'. The sentence conveys that the timers will be removed, and the possible reason is that there might be some problems. Therefore, the noun 'glitches' is the most appropriate choice.
Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

t: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. Even after facing severe criticism, she managed to __________ and continue her work confidently.
e: Explanation: The correct answer is option (3). English Explanation: “Bear up” means to remain strong, cheerful, or courageous in difficult or stressful circumstances. In the sentence, despite facing severe criticism, she stayed mentally strong and continued her work confidently. Therefore, “bear up” correctly conveys the idea of maintaining emotional strength. “Bear down” means to put pressure on or concentrate intensely. “Bear out” means to confirm or support something with evidence. “Bear with” means to be patient with someone. Since the context refers to staying strong during hardship, “bear up” is the most appropriate fit. 1. Bear down (दबाव डालना / ज़ोर लगाना) Meaning in Hindi: पूरी ताकत लगाना या दबाव डालना। Example: The cyclist bore down on the final stretch of the race. (साइकिल चालक ने दौड़ के अंतिम हिस्से में पूरी ताकत लगा दी।) 2. Bear out (पुष्टि करना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी तथ्य की पुष्टि करना। Example: The evidence bore out his statement. (साक्ष्यों ने उसके बयान की पुष्टि की।) 3. Bear up (हिम्मत बनाए रखना) Meaning in Hindi: कठिन परिस्थिति में भी मजबूत बने रहना। Example 1: Despite repeated failures, he bore up well and continued his preparation with determination. (बार-बार असफल होने के बावजूद उसने हिम्मत बनाए रखी और तैयारी जारी रखी।) Example 2: She bore up bravely during the tough times. (उसने कठिन समय में साहस बनाए रखा।) 4. Bear with (धैर्य रखना / सहन करना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी के साथ धैर्य रखना। Example: Please bear with me while I explain the process. (कृपया प्रक्रिया समझाते समय धैर्य रखें।)

t:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.
These were two Indian men who _______ hiding in the forest.
e:
The sentence talks about two Indian men, hence plural verb should be used here. So, 'was', and 'has' cannot be used here.
'Have' is not followed by the -ing form of the verb. So, option (d) is incorrect as well.
The complete sentence is: These were two Indian men who had been hiding in the forest.
Hence, option (c) is the answer.

t:
Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence.
Students were running ___, even though they were required to ____ for their upcoming blood tests.
e:
The correct word to fill in the blanks is 'fast'. 'Fast' as an adverb means quickly or at a high speed. In the first blank, the use of the word 'fast' suggests that the students were running at a high speed. 'Fast' as a verb means to abstain from eating. In the second blank, it implies that the students were required to refrain from eating for their upcoming blood tests. Other options are not suitable for the second blank and are thus negated.
The complete sentence is: Students were running fast, even though they were required to fast for their upcoming blood tests.
Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

t: The following sentence contains blank spaces, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.The stranded hiker began to __________ help when he spotted a rescue helicopter, but he later had to __________ his companion for ignoring the safety protocols that led to their predicament.
e: Rule / Concept: Shout at vs. Shout forIn English grammar, the preposition following "shout" significantly alters the intent of the action:Application to the Given Question"...began to shout for help when he spotted a rescue helicopter, but he later had to shout at his companion for ignoring the safety protocols..."In the first blank, the hiker is calling out to obtain "help" (a request/need), which requires "for". In the second blank, he is expressing anger toward his "companion" (the target of his frustration), which requires "at".Things to Remember / Exam Tips

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Though the bedsheet that they gifted us is not made of wool, it has a _________ texture to it which can be felt after touching.
e:
'Woozy' means unsteady, dizzy, or dazed. 'Woolen' means made of wool. 'Woolish' is an incorrect word.
An adjective is required here to describe the texture of the bedsheet so 'woolen' is the correct adjective to describe that as it is mentioned in the initial part of the sentence that it is not made up of wool.
Hence, option (c) is correct.

t:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.
Johannes Gutenberg invented the first printing press that could print thousands of ______________ a day. This made books
cheaper and information ______________ widely available.
e:
A printing press prints "pages" (standard term for book content). "More widely available" is the correct comparative phrase for information accessibility.
Option (b) sheet; much: "Sheet" is less specific than "pages" for books, and "much" is used for uncountable nouns, not suitable here.
Option (c) leaf; many: "Leaf" is an archaic term for a book page, and "many" is for countable nouns, not fitting "information."
Option (d) sides; most: "Sides" is vague, and "most" implies a superlative, not a comparative increase.

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.
Reptiles _________ from amphibians. For a long period of 160 million years in earth's history, reptiles were the dominant form of life on the planet and _________ in an enormous variety of shapes and sizes.
e: Reptiles "evolved" from amphibians, indicating a gradual development through natural selection, which fits the biological context. The term "evolved" is commonly used in scientific contexts to describe the origin and diversification of species. For the second blank, "existed" is suitable because it conveys that reptiles were present and dominant in a wide variety of forms over a long period, aligning with the idea of their persistence and diversity during that era. Correct sentence: Reptiles evolved from amphibians. For a long period of 160 million years in earth's history, reptiles were the dominant form of life on the planet and existed in an enormous variety of shapes and sizes.

t: The following sentence contains blank spaces, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.While the traditional festival encourages all villagers to ___________ the communal singing, the elders alone are permitted to ___________ the sacred herbal concoction prepared by the priest.
e: Rule / Concept: Partake in vs. Partake ofIn advanced English, the meaning of "partake" shifts significantly based on the preposition:Application to the Given Question"...villagers to partake in the communal singing, the elders alone are permitted to partake of the sacred herbal concoction..."In the first part, the context is "communal singing," which is an activity/event, requiring the preposition "in". In the second part, the context is a "herbal concoction" (a drink), which refers to consumption, requiring the preposition "of". Option A correctly identifies this distinction.Things to Remember / Exam Tips

t: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Many of the _______ we were taught about what is healthy, or ethical, were untrue, and it is time we define new ideas of what it means to lead a good life.
e:
The blank requires a noun in its plural form as it is preceded by the phrase 'many of the'. The determiner 'many' is plural and should be followed by a plural noun. Options b) and c) are eliminated because they are adjectives. Option a) is a noun, but it is singular (and not plural). Therefore, option a) is eliminated. Option d) is a plural noun.
'Lessons' satisfies the grammatical condition mentioned above and correctly fills the blank.
Thus, option d) is correct.

t: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. While preparing the final report, the consultant decided to __________ his years of field experience.
e: Explanation: The correct answer is option (3). English Explanation: “Draw on” means to use or rely on one’s experience, knowledge, skills, or resources. In the sentence, the consultant is using his years of field experience while preparing the final report. Therefore, “draw on” correctly conveys the idea of relying upon or utilizing prior experience. “Draw up” means to prepare or draft something formally. “Draw out” means to encourage someone to speak or to prolong something. “Draw in” means to attract or pull something inward. Since the context refers to using past experience as a resource, “draw on” is the most appropriate fit. 1. Draw up (तैयार करना / मसौदा बनाना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी योजना या दस्तावेज़ को औपचारिक रूप से तैयार करना। Example: The lawyer drew up the agreement carefully. (वकील ने समझौता सावधानी से तैयार किया।) 2. Draw out (बात निकलवाना / लंबा खींचना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी से विचार निकलवाना या किसी प्रक्रिया को लंबा करना। Example: The teacher tried to draw out the shy student during discussion. (शिक्षक ने चर्चा के दौरान शर्मीले छात्र से बात निकलवाने की कोशिश की।) 3. Draw on (उपयोग करना / सहारा लेना) Meaning in Hindi: अनुभव या ज्ञान का उपयोग करना। Example 1: While writing the answer, she drew on her previous knowledge of history. (उत्तर लिखते समय उसने अपने पूर्व इतिहास ज्ञान का उपयोग किया।) Example 2: He drew on his savings to start the business. (उसने व्यवसाय शुरू करने के लिए अपनी बचत का सहारा लिया।) 4. Draw in (आकर्षित करना / अंदर खींचना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी को आकर्षित करना या अंदर की ओर खींचना। Example: The advertisement drew in a large audience. (विज्ञापन ने बड़ी संख्या में दर्शकों को आकर्षित किया।)

t:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank:
The media, these days, constructs ________(misleading) narratives on politics and celebrities to increase the viewership.
e: "Mendacious" means false or misleading, which is the correct synonym for "misleading."

t:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate conjunction. 
He didn't eat properly, ____ fell sick.
e:
'Therefore' is a conjunctive adverb that means for that reason or cause, thus, or consequently. In the given sentence, it's mentioned that the boy didn't pay attention towards his food intake, and as a result, he fell sick. There is a reason given, so 'therefore' is used in the second blank. Hence, (d) is the correct answer. 
The final sentence would be: He didn't eat properly, therefore fell sick.

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Supriya found ____ interesting book at the bookstore.
e: The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is (a). The indefinite article "an" is used before words that begin with a vowel sound. In this sentence, the word "interesting" starts with a vowel sound. So, "an" is a suitable word to use. The indefinite article "a" is used before words that begin with a consonant sound. The definite article "the" is used to specify a particular or previously mentioned noun. In this sentence, there is no prior mention or specific context to warrant the use of "the" before "interesting book." The sentence is more about a general discovery of an interesting book. It does not refer to a specific book known to both the speaker and the listener. Hence, (a) is the correct answer. NOTE: A noun is a word used as the name of a person, place, or thing. Now consider the following sentences: 1) Mahesh is a clever boy. 2) A herd of cattle was grazing on the pastureland. 3) Honesty is the best policy. An article is a word that comes before a noun to indicate whether it's specific or general. Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

t: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. Violence suddenly __________ in the city after the controversial announcement.
e: Explanation: The correct answer is option (3). English Explanation: “Break out” means to begin suddenly, especially in reference to events like war, violence, fire, disease, or chaos. In the sentence, violence suddenly began in the city after the controversial announcement. Therefore, “broke out” correctly conveys the idea of something starting abruptly and unexpectedly. “Break up” means to separate or disperse. “Break down” means to stop functioning or to collapse emotionally. “Break into” means to enter forcibly or suddenly start doing something (like laughing). Since the context refers to violence starting suddenly, “broke out” is the most appropriate fit. 1. Broke up (अलग होना / बिखर जाना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी समूह का बिखर जाना या संबंध का समाप्त होना। Example: The crowd broke up after the speech ended. (भाषण खत्म होने के बाद भीड़ बिखर गई।) 2. Broke down (खराब होना / भावनात्मक रूप से टूट जाना) Meaning in Hindi: मशीन का खराब हो जाना या व्यक्ति का भावनात्मक रूप से टूट जाना। Example: His car broke down on the way to the office. (उसकी गाड़ी दफ्तर जाते समय खराब हो गई।) 3. Broke out (अचानक शुरू होना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी घटना का अचानक शुरू हो जाना। Example 1: A fire broke out in the examination hall due to a short circuit. (शॉर्ट सर्किट के कारण परीक्षा कक्ष में आग लग गई।) Example 2: An argument broke out between the two teams. (दोनों टीमों के बीच अचानक बहस शुरू हो गई।) 4. Broke into (ज़बरदस्ती घुसना / अचानक शुरू करना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी जगह में जबरन प्रवेश करना या अचानक कुछ करना। Example: The thief broke into the house at night. (चोर रात में घर में घुस गया।)

t: The following sentence contains blank spaces, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.During the debate, __________ Principal and __________ Teacher were seen arguing over the new policy.
e: Fill the blanks with the, the.Rule / Concept: Two Nouns referring to Different Persons –When two or more nouns in a sentence refer to different persons, the definite article 'the' must be used before each noun. The most reliable way to identify this in an exam is to look at the verb; a plural verb indicates that the nouns represent distinct individuals.Things to Remember / Exam Tips-The Verb is the Key: Always check the verb (is/was vs. are/were) first. It acts as the signal for how many articles are needed.Pronoun Agreement: If the sentence uses a plural possessive like 'their', it is a strong hint that you are dealing with two separate individuals requiring two articles.

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The mango is the ______ fruit.
e: The sentence implies a superlative quality of the mango compared to other fruits. The superlative form of the adjective "sweet" is "sweetest," indicating the mango is the most sweet among all fruits. "Sweetly" is an adverb, "sweet" is the base adjective, and "sweeter" is comparative, none of which fit the superlative context. Thus, "sweetest" is the correct choice. The complete sentence is: "The mango is the sweetest fruit."

t: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. During the charity event, the organizers decided to __________ free blankets to the homeless.
e: Explanation: The correct answer is option (2). English Explanation: “Give away” means to distribute something for free or to donate something to others. In the sentence, the organizers are distributing free blankets during a charity event. Therefore, “give away” correctly conveys the idea of donating or handing out something without taking payment. “Give in” means to surrender or yield. “Give off” means to emit something like smell, light, or heat. “Give up” means to quit or stop doing something. Since the context is about distributing blankets for free, “give away” is the most appropriate fit. 1. Give in (हार मान लेना) Example: After hours of argument, he finally gave in. (कई घंटों की बहस के बाद वह आखिरकार मान गया।) 2. Give away (मुफ्त में बाँटना / दान करना) Example 1: The company gave away free samples to customers. (कंपनी ने ग्राहकों को मुफ्त सैंपल बाँटे।) Example 2: She gave away her old clothes to the needy. (उसने अपने पुराने कपड़े जरूरतमंदों को दे दिए।) 3. Give off (छोड़ना / उत्सर्जित करना) Example: The flowers give off a pleasant fragrance. (फूल सुगंध छोड़ते हैं।) 4. Give up (छोड़ देना / त्याग देना) Example: He gave up smoking last year. (उसने पिछले साल धूम्रपान छोड़ दिया।)

t: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. When I visited the village, I made sure to __________ my elderly neighbor who had been unwell for weeks.
e: Explanation: The correct answer is option (3). English Explanation: “Ask after” means to inquire about someone’s health or well-being, especially in a caring or polite way. In the sentence, the speaker visited the village and wanted to check on the elderly neighbor who had been unwell. Therefore, “ask after” correctly conveys the idea of inquiring about someone’s condition. “Ask for” means to request something. “Ask about” means to seek information about something in general. “Ask over” means to invite someone to come to your home. Since the context involves politely inquiring about someone’s health, “ask after” is the most appropriate fit. 1. Ask for (मांग करना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी वस्तु या सहायता की मांग करना। Example: She asked for a glass of water. (उसने एक गिलास पानी मांगा।) 2. Ask about (के बारे में पूछना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी विषय के बारे में जानकारी लेना। Example: He asked about the new policy. (उसने नई नीति के बारे में पूछा।) 3. Ask after (कुशलक्षेम पूछना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी की सेहत या हालचाल पूछना। Example 1: The teacher asked after the student who had been absent due to illness. (शिक्षक ने बीमारी के कारण अनुपस्थित छात्र की कुशलक्षेम पूछी।) Example 2: She always asks after her grandparents during phone calls. (वह फोन पर हमेशा अपने दादा-दादी की कुशलक्षेम पूछती है।) 4. Ask over (घर बुलाना / आमंत्रित करना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी को घर आने के लिए आमंत्रित करना। Example: We asked them over for dinner last night. (हमने उन्हें कल रात खाने पर बुलाया।)

t: The following sentence contains blank spaces, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.In the latest contract, the vendor agreed to _________ the school _________ high-speed internet, provided the city could _________ the necessary infrastructure _________ the project.
e: The "Supply" Structural RuleThe following sentence contains blank spaces, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.Example: The vendor agreed to supply the school (Recipient) with internet (Item).Example: The city could supply infrastructure (Item) for the project (Purpose).Application to the Given Question"...the vendor agreed to supply the school [1] _________ high-speed internet, provided the city could supply the necessary infrastructure [2] _________ the project."

t: The following sentence contains blank spaces, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.The quarterly revenue of the startup was __________ that of its primary competitor to identify market gaps, even though the two business models were fundamentally __________ each other in terms of scalability.
e: Rule / Concept: Compared with vs. Compared toApplication to the Given Question"...revenue of the startup was compared with that of its primary competitor... business models were fundamentally compared to each other..."In the first blank, "compared" is the main verb (passive) used for a formal business analysis of two similar entities (revenues), requiring "with". In the second blank, "compared" is used as a participial adjective describing the state of the business models in a general sense, requiring "to". Option B correctly identifies this structural and functional shift.Things to Remember / Exam Tips

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
I ___ to school daily on foot but my friends prefer to travel by rickshaw.
e: The usage of the word 'daily' indicates a routine and that the sentence is in the Present Simple tense [indicated by the use of the present tense verb 'prefer']. So, the present tense form of the verb (go) is used in the blank. The past tense verbs 'went' and 'gone' and the present continuous tense verb 'going' are eliminated. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Currently, Mittu and Bittu ____ hard to meet the project deadline.
e:
The adverb "currently" indicates that the action is happening now, requiring the present continuous tense ("are working"). Mittu and Bittu are the plural subject, and "are working" correctly describes their ongoing effort to meet the deadline. The other tenses do not align with the present time frame indicated by "currently."
Worked: The simple past tense "worked" indicates a completed action, not an ongoing one, which conflicts with "currently."
Have worked: The present perfect tense "have worked" suggests a completed action with present relevance, not an ongoing action.
Were working: The past continuous tense "were working" indicates an ongoing action in the past, not the present.
The complete sentence: Currently, Mittu and Bittu are working hard to meet the project deadline.
Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

t:
Select the present perfect tense of the verb given in the brackets to fill in the blank. 
Alex _______ (study) two programming languages.
e: The present perfect tense describes an action that happened at an unspecified time in the past or has relevance to the present. It is formed using "has/have" + past participle. The subject, "Alex," is singular, so "has" is appropriate. · (1) Has studied: This is the present perfect tense, using "has" (singular) and the past participle "studied." It indicates that Alex completed studying two programming languages at some point, with relevance to now (e.g., he knows them). This fits the sentence. · (2) Have study: This is incorrect because "have" requires a plural subject, and "study" is the base form, not the past participle needed for present perfect (correct: "studied"). · (3) Has been studying: This is the present perfect continuous tense, emphasizing an ongoing action that started in the past and continues. The sentence doesn't suggest ongoing study, so this is less appropriate. · (4) Had studied: This is the past perfect tense, used for actions completed before another past event, which doesn't match the present relevance implied by the sentence. The sentence implies a completed action with present relevance, making has studied the correct present perfect form. Therefore, the correct answer is option (1).

t: Given the critical nature of the diplomatic mission, it is imperative that the envoy __________ with the Prime Minister to discuss the escalating border tensions before the international summit begins.
e: The Correct Ans is Option (D). 📌 Rule / Concept: The Present Subjunctive Mood (Imperative Adjectives) The Present Subjunctive is used in "that-clauses" following adjectives that express necessity, urgency, or importance (e.g., imperative, essential, vital, crucial, necessary). In this formal mood, the verb in the "that-clause" must be in its base form (the infinitive without "to"), even if the subject is third-person singular (he, she, it, or a singular noun). 💢 Application to the Given Question - The adjective imperative acts as the trigger. The subject of the following clause is "the envoy" (singular). While standard grammar would require "meets," the subjunctive mood demands the base form meet.

t: He seldom questions the directives issued by the regulatory authority, ______?
e: The Correct Ans is Option (D) - “does he”. 📌 Rule / Concept: Negative Meaning Word (“Seldom”) + Do-Support Words like seldom, rarely, hardly, scarcely make a sentence negative in meaning. When the statement is negative in meaning → the question tag must be positive. If the main clause does not contain an auxiliary verb, we use do-support (do/does/did) according to tense. 💢 Application to the Given Question He seldom questions the directives issued by the regulatory authority “Seldom” → negative meaning Therefore → tag must be positive Main verb = questions (simple present) No auxiliary present → use do-support Subject = he → use does So, the correct tag is: does he? ✅ More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅- She rarely complains about workload, does she? Example 2 ✅- They hardly participate in discussions, do they? Example 3 ✅ - He scarcely acknowledges his mistakes, does he? 🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips Seldom = negative meaning Negative meaning → positive tag No auxiliary in main clause → use do-support Match tense carefully (questions → does)

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Rohan is _______ self-sufficient man who needs no assistance.
e: The blank will be filled with the indefinite article 'a' as the sentence mentions the singular subject 'Rohan' to be self-sufficient. The definite article 'the' is not used before the adjectives unless we use it with adjectives like rich, poor, elderly, and unemployed to talk about groups of people. In ('used to indicate location or position within or inside something') does not fit in contextually as no location or position is mentioned in the sentence. Of ('expresses the relationship between a part and a whole') renders the sentence meaningless contextually. Hence, option (b) is the answer. The correct sentence is: Rohan is a self-sufficient man who needs no assistance. Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

t:
Complete the collocation.
I met my professor yesterday and we _____ a long conversation about books and work.
e: In the English language, collocation refers to a natural combination of words that are closely affiliated with each other. 'Have a conversation' - If you have a conversation with someone, you talk with them, usually in an informal situation. So, with 'conversation', we generally use the verb 'had'. 'Did a conversation', 'spoke a conversation', and 'talked a conversation' are not correct phrases. The correct sentence is: I met my professor yesterday and we had a long conversation about books and work. Hence, option (c) is the answer.

t:
Fill in the blank with a suitable adjective. 
Anamika is the smartest and _____ of all students.
e:
Two adjectives which refer to the same noun or pronoun joined by conjunction must be in the same degree of comparison. So, the blank will be filled by a superlative form of adjective. Hence, (c) is the correct answer. 
The final sentence will be: Anamika is the smartest and kindest of all students.

t:
Select the most appropriate tense form to fill in the blank.
Tania ____ to the canteen.
e:
The sentence lacks context for time, but the options suggest a past tense. "Tania" is singular, so the singular past continuous "was going" is appropriate, indicating an ongoing action in the past (e.g., Tania was on her way to the canteen). The other options are either incorrect in number or grammatically invalid.
"Were gone" is plural and implies completion, not an ongoing action.
"Were going" is plural, incorrect for the singular subject "Tania."
"Had going" is not a valid verb form in English.
The complete sentence: Tania was going to the canteen.
Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Prerna is the leader of the ladies' wing. So, while asking the opinions of the legislators, the principal asked _____ as well.
e:
Options (a) and (b) are eliminated as they correspond to a male. A subjective pronoun cannot be used here because the pronoun in the blank is the objective case of the verb 'asked'. The blank should be replaced with a possessive pronoun as the principal asked for Prerna's opinion. So, 'hers' is the most appropriate choice. 
Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

t:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.
If it _______ been for him, nobody would even have known Monster was back!
e:
The third conditional uses the past perfect ('had not been' in the given sentence) in the if clause and a modal ('would' in the given sentence) and present perfect ('have known' in the given sentence) in the result clause. This form is used to talk about a hypothetical situation in the past that did not happen - typically with an outcome that did not happen and is perhaps the opposite of what did happen. The same is the scenario here. 
So, the complete sentence is: If it hadn't been for him, nobody would even have known Monster was back!
Hence, option (b) is the answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate adverb to fill in the blank.
Nitha can assemble the students of her class ______.
e:
The blank requires an adverb to modify the action 'assemble the students'.
So, options (a) [adjective] and (b) [verb] are incorrect.
'Slow' as an adverb means 'at a slow pace; slowly'. But it does not fit in the blank as the sentence aims to denote the ability of Nitha. Anyone can assemble the students if given a lot of time. So, option (c) is incorrect.
The correct adverb to be used here is 'quickly'. It's Nitha's ability that she can quickly assemble the students of her class.
Hence, option (d) is the answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. 
Magnets have a special _____ to attract certain materials, particularly those containing iron, nickel, or cobalt, due to their magnetic fields. They ____ through the force of magnetism, which is created by the alignment of tiny magnetic particles within the magnet.
e:
The most appropriate option to fill in the first blank is 'ability'. 'Ability' means the quality of being able to do something, especially the physical, mental, financial, or legal power to accomplish something. In the sentence, it indicates that magnets possess a special power or capability to attract specific materials, emphasising their unique property due to their magnetic fields. Other words do not fit the context of the sentence. 'Fragility' means being easily broken or damaged. 'Error' means a mistake. 'Guilt' means a feeling of having committed wrong or failed in an obligation.
The most appropriate option to fill in the second blank is 'work'. In the sentence, 'work' describes how magnets function or operate through the force of magnetism, explaining the mechanism behind their ability to attract certain materials. Other words do not fit the context of the sentence. 'Study' means to devote time and attention to gaining knowledge. 'Stir' means to mix or move around. 'Beat' means to strike repeatedly. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

t:
Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank.
In 2030, advancements in technology _______ the way we live, work and interact with each other.
e:
The sentence refers to a future event in 2030, describing the ongoing impact of technological advancements. The appropriate verb tense should reflect future action with a continuous effect.
Option 1("could be reshaped") suggests possibility but lacks the certainty implied by the context.
Option 2 ("shall have been reshaped") is a future perfect tense, implying completion by 2030, which doesn't fit the ongoing nature.
Option 3 ("will be reshaping") is the future continuous tense, indicating ongoing action in the future, which suits the context of continuous change.
Option 4 ("have reshaped") is present perfect, implying past action, which is incorrect for a future context.
Thus, "will be reshaping" is the most appropriate choice.

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Garima has already finished her homework, __________?
e: The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is 'hasn't she'. When the main sentence/clause is positive, the question tag should be negative, and vice versa. In the given case, the main sentence/clause is positive. So, the question tag would be negative. Also, if there is an auxiliary verb (be, have, do, is, etc.) in the main sentence/clause, the question tag also contains the same auxiliary verb. In the given sentence, the auxiliary verb "has" is used. Accordingly, option (a) is correct because it maintains the opposite polarity (positive main sentence, negative question tag) and uses the same auxiliary verb ("has"). Option (b) is incorrect as it changes the pronoun to "he" and uses "isn't," which is not consistent with the original sentence. Option (c) is incorrect because it uses "wasn't", which is not consistent with the original auxiliary verb "has." Option (d) is also incorrect. This option uses "doesn't", which is not consistent with the original auxiliary verb "has." The forms of 'do' (does, do, did) are used when there is no auxiliary verb in the main clause. When forming question tags, if the main clause lacks an auxiliary verb (be, have, can, will, etc.), a suitable form of "do" is introduced in the question tag. Hence, (a) is the correct answer. NOTE: Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

t: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s). In some rural areas in India, the hospitals are ___ equipped because of the ___ of the funds from the administration.
e:
The correct choice is option (c) inadequately, scarcity.
· Inadequately: Insufficient, inept, or unsuitable; Scarcity: Insufficiency or shortness of supply.
· Among the given options, option (c) fits the best in the context of the sentence. The sentence refers to the scarcity of equipment and funds in the hospitals in some rural areas. 'Faulty' is an adjective and cannot be used in the first blank because an adverb is needed to qualify the adjective 'equipped'. The rest of the options are incorrect because no hospital can be 'well/fully equipped' because of a lack of funds. Both 'dearth' and 'paucity' means 'shortage'.

t: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. As the investigation progressed, the authorities began to __________ the prime suspect.
e: Explanation: The correct answer is option (3). English Explanation: “Close in on” means to move nearer to someone or something in order to surround, capture, or approach it closely. It can also be used metaphorically for pressure or deadlines approaching. In the sentence, as the investigation progressed, the authorities were moving nearer to the prime suspect, possibly to surround or apprehend him. Therefore, “close in on” correctly conveys the idea of gradually approaching or tightening around someone. “Close up” means to shut something or become temporarily unavailable. “Close out” means to end or finish something, especially an account or business. “Close down” means to permanently stop operations. Since the context refers to authorities approaching a suspect, “close in on” is the most appropriate fit. 1. Close up (बंद करना / अस्थायी रूप से बंद होना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी चीज़ को बंद करना। Example: The shop closed up early due to heavy rain. (भारी बारिश के कारण दुकान जल्दी बंद हो गई।) 2. Close out (समाप्त करना / निपटाना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी खाते या कार्य को पूरी तरह समाप्त करना। Example: The company decided to close out the old accounts. (कंपनी ने पुराने खातों को बंद करने का निर्णय लिया।) 3. Close in on (करीब पहुँचकर घेरना / दबाव बढ़ना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी के पास जाकर उसे घेर लेना या दबाव का पास आना। Example 1: As the deadline approached, pressure began to close in on the candidates. (समयसीमा नज़दीक आने पर उम्मीदवारों पर दबाव बढ़ने लगा।) Example 2: The police closed in on the criminal after a long chase. (लंबे पीछा करने के बाद पुलिस अपराधी के करीब पहुँच गई।) 4. Close down (स्थायी रूप से बंद करना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी संस्था या व्यवसाय को हमेशा के लिए बंद कर देना। Example: The factory was closed down due to heavy losses. (भारी घाटे के कारण फैक्ट्री बंद कर दी गई।)

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The professor __________ explained the concept for the fifth time with a smiling face to the class.
e: Among the given options, "indulgently" fits the context of the sentence. It gives us the idea that with a smile on his face, the professor, in a generous manner, conveyed the concept to the class for the fifth time. Indulgently: having or indicating a readiness or over-readiness to be generous to or lenient with someone. The word that must fit the blank should be an adverb because it is modifying 'explained' (verb). 'Friendly' is an adjective and thus, it is an incorrect option. 'Intolerantly' and 'repulsively' are contextual misfits because the professor explained a concept with 'a smiling face' and this hints at his generous nature. Thus, the correct option is (b), indulgently. Thus, the correct sentence should be: The professor indulgently explained the concept for the fifth time with a smiling face to the class. Additional Information: The respective meanings of the other options are given below in the table:WordMeaningIntolerantlynot tolerant of views, beliefs, or behaviourFriendlykind and pleasantRepulsivelydisgustedly

t: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. Stop trying to __________ me by making fun of my presentation; it’s not funny anymore.
e: Explanation: The correct answer is option (2). English Explanation: “Wind up” (informal usage) means to tease, irritate, or deliberately provoke someone, often in a playful way. In the sentence, the speaker is asking someone to stop making fun of their presentation, which shows irritation caused by teasing. Therefore, “wind up” correctly conveys the idea of provoking or irritating someone. “Wind down” means to relax or gradually come to an end. “Wind off” is not commonly used in this context and generally relates to removing something wound around an object. “Wind out” can mean to knock the breath out of someone but does not fit the idea of teasing. Since the context refers to irritating someone through teasing, “wind up” is the most appropriate fit. 1. Wind down (धीरे-धीरे शांत होना / समाप्त होना) Meaning in Hindi: आराम करना या धीरे-धीरे किसी गतिविधि को समाप्त करना। Example: After the meeting, we wound down with some light music. (बैठक के बाद हमने हल्का संगीत सुनकर आराम किया।) 2. Wind up (चिढ़ाना / परेशान करना; समाप्त करना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी को चिढ़ाना या किसी कार्य को समाप्त करना। Example 1: His friends were just winding him up by joking about the exam results. (उसके दोस्त परीक्षा परिणामों पर मज़ाक करके उसे चिढ़ा रहे थे।) Example 2: She wound up the discussion after two hours. (उसने दो घंटे बाद चर्चा समाप्त कर दी।) 3. Wind off (लपेट हटाना / निकालना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी चीज़ को लपेट से हटाना या निकालना। Example: He wound off the tape from the old recorder. (उसने पुराने रिकॉर्डर से टेप निकाल लिया।) 4. Wind out (सांस निकाल देना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी की सांस निकाल देना या जोर से चोट लगना। Example: The punch nearly winded him out. (घूंसे से उसकी लगभग सांस निकल गई।)

t:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
For everyone, the Winter _______ back warm and homely sentiments of their juvenility, and they often go back to the _________ of nostalgia that they had during those frosty but comfortable and joyful nights, hence, winter vacations should be ________ by doing unforgettable activities _______ family, cousins, and friends.
e:
The paragraph is about remembering wintertime and its beautiful memories.
Blank 1: 'Brings back' means cause something to return to the mind.
'Drives back' means fight off or force which is not related to the context, so it is incorrect. 'Guide' is a plural verb so it cannot be used with the singular noun 'winter'. So, options (b) and (d) will be eliminated.
Blank 2: The use of 'herd' for nostalgia/memories is incorrect as 'herd' means a large number of animals that live and feed together. Similarly, the use of 'convoy' is also incorrect as it means a group of vehicles or ships travelling together. So, both are contextually incorrect. So, options (c) and (d) are incorrect.
In blanks 3 and 4, the use of 'spent' and 'with' [in the company of] is justified as it brings out the meaning that one should have quality time with family and friends during winter.
'Brings, lane, spent, with' is the right set of words for the blanks.
Hence, option (a) is correct.

t:
Select the most appropriate adverb to fill in the blank.
___, I'm going to walk my dog.
e:
The sentence requires an adverb that indicates the timing of the action "walk my dog." "Now" is an adverb of time meaning at the present moment, which fits perfectly: "I'm going to walk my dog." It indicates immediate action.
The complete sentence: Now, I'm going to walk my dog.
(b) Already: "Already" indicates something has happened before the present moment (e.g., "I've already walked my dog"). It doesn't suit a future intention ("going to").
(c) Annually: "Annually" means once a year, which is inappropriate for a routine action like walking a dog, implying an unrealistic frequency.
(d) Rarely: "Rarely" indicates infrequency, which contradicts the context of planning to walk the dog immediately.
Hence, the correct answer is option (1).

t: I condoled.......my friend with the death of his father.
e:
The verb condole is followed by “with” when expressing sympathy to a person.
✔ Correct usages:



I condoled with her on her loss.


We condoled with the bereaved family.

t:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The Transport Corporation has decided to discontinue ______ bus service for private schools.
e: 'Bus service' is a singular noun phrase, so we can eliminate the plural demonstrative adjectives 'these' and 'those'. We need a possessive determiner to qualify the noun 'bus service'. "It's" is the contracted form of "it is/it has" which is not required here. So, option (a) is eliminated as it is grammatically incorrect. The possessive determiner 'its' is the one that fits correctly in the blank. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer. Note: Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books." Demonstrative Adjectives: Demonstrative adjectives include "this", "that", "these" and "those". These modify or describe a noun and come before a noun while 'demonstrative pronouns' replace a noun. Example: "I like that T-shirt of yours".

t: The following sentence contains blank spaces, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.The defendant was found _________ the heist by the jury, but even after his release, he continued to feel _________ the trauma he had caused the victims.
e: RuleApplication to the Given Question"The defendant was found [1] guilty of the heist... he continued to feel [2] guilty about the trauma..."First Blank: The context is a jury's verdict regarding a "heist" (a crime). This is a statement of legal fact, requiring the preposition "of."Second Blank: The context is the person's internal "feelings" regarding the "trauma" (remorse). Since it describes a psychological state of regret, we use "about."

t: She used to handle the arbitration cases independently, ______?
e: The Correct Ans is Option (C) - “didn’t she”. 📌 Rule / Concept: “Used to” Structure in Question Tags When “used to” expresses a past habit, it behaves like a simple past structure, not like a modal verb. Therefore, the question tag must use: did / didn’t + subject 💢 Application to the Given Question - She used to handle the arbitration cases independently This describes a past habit. So, the correct tag must use didn’t, because: Tense = Past Auxiliary needed = did Subject = she Hence: didn’t she? ✅ More Examples for Clarity Example 1 ✅ - He used to work late hours, didn’t he? Example 2 ✅ - They used to travel frequently, didn’t they? Example 3 ✅ - The firm used to outsource its legal work, didn’t it? 🧠 Things to Remember “Used to” = past habit → use didn’t in tag. Treat it like simple past for tag formation.

t: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. The new leadership aims to __________ significant changes in the organization’s work culture.
e: Explanation: The correct answer is option (2). English Explanation: “Bring about” means to cause something to happen or to make something occur. In the sentence, the new leadership aims to cause significant changes in the organization’s work culture. Therefore, “bring about” correctly conveys the idea of producing or initiating change. “Bring up” means to raise a topic or to nurture a child. “Bring out” means to reveal, publish, or highlight something. “Bring in” means to introduce or earn something. Since the context refers to causing major changes, “bring about” is the most appropriate fit. 1. Bring up (उठाना / पालन-पोषण करना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी विषय को चर्चा में लाना या बच्चे का पालन-पोषण करना। Example: She brought up an important issue during the meeting. (उसने बैठक में एक महत्वपूर्ण मुद्दा उठाया।) 2. Bring about (उत्पन्न करना / कारण बनना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी परिवर्तन या घटना का कारण बनना। Example 1: The new education policy is expected to bring about major reforms in the examination system. (नई शिक्षा नीति से परीक्षा प्रणाली में बड़े सुधार होने की उम्मीद है।) Example 2: Technological advancements have brought about rapid development. (तकनीकी प्रगति ने तेज़ विकास को जन्म दिया है।) 3. Bring out (प्रकट करना / प्रकाशित करना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी चीज़ को उजागर करना या प्रकाशित करना। Example: The author brought out a new novel last month. (लेखक ने पिछले महीने एक नई उपन्यास प्रकाशित की।) 4. Bring in (लाना / आय अर्जित करना) Meaning in Hindi: किसी चीज़ को अंदर लाना या कमाई करना। Example: The new product brought in huge profits. (नए उत्पाद ने भारी मुनाफा कमाया।)

t:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.
I _______ something burning now.
e:
The completed sentence would then be: "I smell something burning now."
This sentence is in the present tense and describes the action of smelling something in the present moment.
Hence, option (a) is correct.

t:
Select the appropriate option for the given blank.
The invitations have been kept ____ the table.
e:
The blank requires an adverb of place to denote the position of the invitation with respect to the table. Accordingly, only option (a), 'on' is an adverb of place and so, it can fill the blank as required. 'Randomly' and 'sequentially' are adverbs of manner, 'often' is an adverb of frequency and 'when' is an adverb of interrogation and so, these options are negated.
The complete sentence is: The invitations have been kept on the table.
Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

t: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. She suddenly __________ a severe cold a day before her presentation.
